raw_response:
I’m an old hand at this now, and on just 3 mu I cannot take big risks. What I do is mostly the same wheat-maize rotation as before, because that keeps grain coming and spreads the risk. I only finished with wheat not long before maize goes in, so the field turnaround has to be quick. Money matters more than chasing the very highest yield. If I use too little fertilizer, the crop looks weak and I lose more than I save, but I also cannot spend too much because there are only two of us at home and some family labor is away working outside. So I’ll use a moderate amount, about what worked in past years, and watch the crop. If the wheat seedlings come up well, I’ll stay with my usual plan. If the leaves turn yellow after winter, I’ll add a bit more topdressing. For irrigation, since we have well water, I’ll use it at the important stages, but not too many times because pumping costs money. I don’t like changing seed often. I’ll buy local wheat seed and maize hybrid that people nearby use, the kind I know can grow steadily here.
